## Sen. Mitch McConnell to Step Down in November
[Sen. Mitch McConnell of Kentucky](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJxskLFuwyAUAL8GNiL8_GzMwNCFLV07WgSeAxUGy6BY_fuq7dr5TjrpPu7r3aWcyvPd7WT6Vlfne3rRCgK0AFyRB7MRAY2czKCkhkEhTDwa5dCHB03KK1i0HzyMyzZLdIPUfpkVTwYkoATQg5zmSd78GBZJckT3mNEND4aSQur1vH3WVHqkLX_VF503X3eeTez9aGx8Y2AZ2B4pppx_GAMb606FrsbANiquEwOLqHEaZ7F7X0uhnEWvonU6RKhXEa6JP1U86yEyuUAnA8tPE44r5ZzarBjK5-7Sb4X3f398BwAA__-dLmE6) announced Wednesday that he would step down as the Republican leader in the Senate this November. McConnell,[ the longest-serving caucus leader](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJxskL1urTAQhJ_GdEZmbTAULm5Dd26bEhl7OTjyDzIbUN4-InW6kWY0-vR9vJaXDTHk93-b0NBWFusoXLgAh4mDWlTjzYYIKBs0nRYTdFpB3-xm6MdVqmHzYpz8NABIqaXuvB57hzDpJhgQoATA1Il-6EXrpB8FCqnsOijbrUwJ9IFKbT9LyLTjFr_LhbV1JTXR7ETHyeQ_BjOD-b7v1uXVPSWD-blmMAt48shgToHczpNzJWeMkVPhJ-HBfbkztyeveHytMTib-YnZEvKI1mPlIfNcLkwr1mdUKrU7pdhU4487xBjOQTMl3smG-EtGf3r6CQAA__8fXmk3) in history, took office in 1985 and plans to serve out his current term, which ends in 2027. McConnell was sometimes emotional [in his address](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJxskL1urTAQhJ_GdEZmbTAULm5Dd26bEhl7OTjyDzIbUN4-InW6kWY0-vR9vJaXDTHk93-b0NBWFusoXLgAh4mDWlTjzYYIKBs0nRYTdFpB3-xm6MdVqmHzYpz8NABIqaXuvB57hzDpJhgQoATA1Il-6EXrpB8FCqnsOijbrUwJ9IFKbT9LyLTjFr_LhbV1JTXR7ETHyeQ_BjOD-b7v1uXVPSWD-blmMAt48shgToHczpNzJWeMkVPhJ-HBfbkztyeveHytMTib-YnZEvKI1mPlIfNcLkwr1mdUKrU7pdhU4487xBjOQTMl3smG-EtGf3r6CQAA__8fXmk3) but did not offer any specific reasons for the timing of his decision, except for the death of his wife's youngest sister. _" To serve Kentucky, has been the honor of my life; to lead my Republican colleagues has been the highest privilege,_" McConnell said.
## Texas Wildfire Now Larger than Rhode Island
[The Smokehouse Creek wildfire](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJxskLFugzAQQL8GNqLzcbbx4KFLtnTtiC7mHK5yAIGbtH9fpXPHp7c8vY_LeGEtutze-S6x5nXkVPUhI3YYOqSR2ilmEZS-lWg8BDSe0LZzDM5loQGCgE9gTWJLibJj9gNzxlYjAhIgBgPWWTilfhpAoCe-OmJzbQhk0rrup89VlzpLLj_rQ_ZTWu9tiXOt29H0bw2eGzzztsjzeKkX7FVTkQbPVb756DZeZl6mIl3WXTp5cPriqutydJh46n02ZAdz5eSJexdMcIGZc7Cu3eO0PbUUPZxvCG531vJXUP_98RsAAP__2JBgnA), the second-largest fire in Texas history, has consumed more than 500,000 acres of land, homes, and businesses since Monday, causing power outages and forcing evacuations across several counties. The fire has expanded to more than 1,300 square miles, larger than the state of Rhode Island, and has spread to parts of neighboring state Oklahoma. [For details, video, and a fire map, click here.](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJxskLHOozAQhJ_GdEbrxWAoKK6hy7VXogUvwYmxEXbC5e1PRLru72Y0I32a-XMbb-S8C_fftHGflzjSnN2bR5TYSdSjLmy_MCNXBffKQIfKaKyLtQc0UzsZO9lFdV2l2g5VU1E7K1N1AHXhegTUgNgpqJsayrmyLTBUmqZGk5qEBrYux6N8RBfyyov_xDcf5Ry3wvdrznsS1S-Bg8DhPM8yZcqcNgpXQ-CQcjw-AofAZ_payixwuLACB8BLG4FD5r-U5Om8XdzBcqNd7hRWCtazTFt88hpfieV8MD_l6YL9SMuvmeX9oJ3l24X_4ePlHWe5U7qIBk3dYKMBLkxx9HY_nfcuNUZouG_k_HdM_vHafwEAAP__GVp5Ug) Texas Governor Greg Abbot issued a [disaster declaration](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJxskLtuhDAQAL_GdEZmMa_CRRq6S5sSLXjNbeTDJ3sDyd9HurSpRxqN5uO23JAjH_s7PshJSAtuwictoGHSYBdbeReIgNqKXDOYCZrBQlfd3dpRaLphDH1As5l2GjBMYGygbWzGDip2YMAagKkxXd-Zemv9aMi0FtfeYrMqa8izpFx_Jj7kTiH-pJNyvaVHFd1d5FlU-6ZgVjDv6ayFvrHUezoVzAddRcH8TEX-KOUjZY3rmkQ0l_JFRXsuWISy9rRFzCicDh1S1i-Tvjj6wJlKlZ1_Xhwjl35Q1uwP5PjKkH-n_AYAAP__qexmGQ) for 60 counties and activated several state emergency response resources to help fight the blaze. [No deaths](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJxskLFugzAQQL8GNqLzcbbx4KFLtnTtiC7mHK5yAIGbtH9fpXPHp7c8vY_LeGEtutze-S6x5nXkVPUhI3YYOqSR2ilmEZS-lWg8BDSe0LZzDM5loQGCgE9gTWJLibJj9gNzxlYjAhIgBgPWWTilfhpAoCe-OmJzbQhk0rrup89VlzpLLj_rQ_ZTWu9tiXOt29H0bw2eGzzztsjzeKkX7FVTkQbPVb756DZeZl6mIl3WXTp5cPriqutydJh46n02ZAdz5eSJexdMcIGZc7Cu3eO0PbUUPZxvCG531vJXUP_98RsAAP__2JBgnA) have been reported, but numerous schools have closed, and some have reopened as emergency shelters for those who lost homes or escaped the fire.
## Google Calls Its 'Woke' AI Tool 'Unacceptable"
Google CEO Sundar Pichai told employees that the "politically correct" responses given by the company's Gemini AI platform were "unacceptable" and that Google was working non-stop to fix it. [His full memo is here.](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJxskLuOrDAQBb_GZEZ2Yx4OHNyEbG66IWqbHvCqsRF4Bs3fr9h4syMdqVSqr8f0wMgxLf9xI1eeecJQ4psmkGAlmMlUs3sSATUVOd0rC7o30FarszhY33bKA9oe7YBt2xkYBj1rBN31VXSgwCgAq1XbtaoOzTwoUo1B3xnUXhhFcyz5qL9zTGWlJ3_ym4465K1it5ayn6L5J2AUMF7XVYfkw30KGG-0gFHBvQcB45LzwiQDZVmI-ZS07Zw_RKdcaIspSozS8yvNdMhXwhBoL-iZ6rVsXB1u3q_IHM-uF0YtG0b-9Sh_VvkJAAD___CsYoU) The Gemini tool was suspended after it refused to show images of white males and instead placed people of color into historically inaccurate contexts. It did no better with text answers. Asked if it was OK to misgender a trans celebrity if it stopped a nuclear apocalypse, it replied that [misgendering would "never" be acceptable. ](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJxsz7Fu6yAUgOGnwRvW4YDNZWC4i7d07WhhOBhaHCIbBeXtq3Tu_A2__s_benO55Pv-4Q6yLdbV-ZaftCJHw1Gtagg2EiHJgazQYFBohdOQLMhtijhHECiMlwSIwRuvJc4xbF4N2SKgAkQjYJonGL0M_4BAKrfNyomNKaCQWz3Hr5rvLVEsr_qkc_T1GIpNrT0uJv8zXBguvffx5VKtb2W43KlfDJdGPr01vfhe617o4r1-E3eZP866FTo4AAhh9KTH1I4ynDY8ei4lX7NmCvbD5fJbbH_-_wQAAP__qF1bUA)It also said there was no clear answer on whether Elon Musk posting memes was worse than Hitler killing millions. Pichai called the issues "problematic" and admitted "they have offended our users and shown bias."

body:

If you've been led to believe that peanut butter, almonds and spinach are good for you, today's email might shock you and is important to read, because these 3 healthy foods could be contributing to health problems in your body.

Let's take a quick look at why...

**1\. Peanut butter**

While peanut butter does contain a small amount of protein and vitamins/minerals, the cons outweigh the pros on this food.

First of all, peanuts contain one of the highest concentrations of aflatoxin, which is a mold toxin that is created in peanuts due to storage in moist conditions.

Peanut butter is also very high in inflammatory omega-6 fats and due to the processing of peanut butter, those omega 6 fats are in a harmful oxidized state.

Most people already get too much omega 6 fats from vegetable oils (soy, corn, canola, etc), and this contributes to insulin resistance, heart disease, brain inflammation, cancer, and lots more health problems, since most people are currently eating 5-10x more omega-6 fats than we should be eating in a healthy diet.

Lastly, peanut butter also contains medium amounts of oxalates, which are plant-based antinutrients that when consumed in excess can contribute to kidney stones, thyroid and gut problems, joint problems and more.

We'll talk more about oxalates in the next food...

**2\. Spinach**

Spinach is promoted as a healthy green, but contains FAR more downsides than good sides. Spinach is one of the highest oxalate foods that's commonly eaten by modern humans (in addition to beet greens, beets, almonds, and other veggies and nuts).

The amount of oxalates in a serving of spinach is extremely high, up to 600 mg in a normal sized bowl.

The "safe" amount of oxalates in a daily diet according to world renowned oxalate expert Sally Norton should be between 100-200 mg per day total to avoid a lot of the health problems caused by high oxalate plants.

So, you can see how concerning spinach is with the extremely high oxalate levels.

As mentioned above, eating too much oxalates too frequently can cause serious issues such as kidney stones, thyroid problems, gut damage, skin issues, and joint pain.

In fact, some people have even gotten "oxalate poisoning" by eating green smoothies too often and had to go to the ER for kidney failure.

**3\. Almonds**

Although almonds and almond milk are marketed as healthy, they also contain many downsides, including all of the negatives mentioned above about too much omega 6 fats and too much oxalates.

They're probably ok in your diet occasionally, but I personally avoid eating almonds too often because of these issues with excess oxalates and omega 6 fats.

Now let's take a look at a fun little quiz below and a few more foods...

**Bananas vs oranges vs apples... (the #1 WORST fruit for your gut & energy)**
According to the best-selling author and world-renowned heart surgeon, Dr. Steven Gundry, there's one fruit people over 40 should never eat.

This fruit can **damage your gut and disrupt your hormones**. Both sapping you of energy and **forcing your body to create "sticky" fat cells that can NOT be "burned off" with normal diet and exercise. **

Right now, the future for unborn babies hangs in the balance in America.

name: Elizabeth Warren
subject: Why I’m asking if you can make a donation today
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Warren for Senate
body:

Here are three reasons why I’m about to ask if you can make a donation to our re-election campaign right now:
1. A Republican from Rhode Island just announced that he’s running against me for Senate in Massachusetts, and he’s reportedly kickstarting his campaign with $500,000 of his own money.
2. Powerful interests and the GOP will be eager to support him and ensure Republican control of the U.S. Senate — I’m not afraid of a tough fight, but we must be prepared for what they’ll throw at us.
3. Tonight’s our first monthly grassroots fundraising deadline since his campaign launch, and we need to respond to his announcement with the strongest possible amount of grassroots donations.

[**If it makes sense for you right now, will you pitch in $28 or any amount to support our re-election campaign and help grow this grassroots movement? Side by side, we’re putting power in the hands of working people, not billionaires and giant corporations — and we’ve got to be ready to fight back against anything that comes our way in this election.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/1908?amount=28&t=8&akid=1947%2E4032634%2Ew0FhoU)

Make no mistake: corporate interests and right-wing extremists would love to see me out of the U.S. Senate. But it isn’t really because of me. It’s because what you and I are building together, alongside people all over the country. It’s because we’ve made real change, from taxing giant corporations to canceling student debt to lowering the cost of hearing aids. And it’s because we’re ready to make even more, from taxing fortunes greater than $50 million to ensuring universal child care to bringing down the cost of housing. We can make it all happen if we keep working together. So I’m asking if you can take another step by my side with a donation today. [**Please chip in any amount you can to respond to my opponent’s announcement and help put Washington on the side of working families.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/1908?t=14&akid=1947%2E4032634%2Ew0FhoU) Thanks for being a part of this, Elizabeth

disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY TEAM KENNEDY
body:
It’s been the purpose of my campaign, to put aside the divisions and solve the real problems.

[](https://www.kennedy24.com/malcolm-x-video?e=d33e868971601c1c714cfe0555abd394&utm_source=joinkennedy&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=malcom_x_2_29_24_rs_nd3&n=4)
---
|
---
Dear Peter,
I recently visited the home of Malcolm X in Queens, New York, which was firebombed a week before his assassination on February 21st, 1965.
Along with my uncle, my father, and Martin Luther King, it was one of four assassinations of the 1960s that devastated the soul of our nation.
Malcolm’s death was especially tragic because it came at a moment where the arc of his life had swung toward viewing all people as part of the brotherhood of humanity.
The central revelation that transformed him was a trip to Mecca where he saw people of every race, creed and color worshiping in the same places and praying to the same god.
After that, he saw his life’s mission as being a truth teller:
_“I’m speaking now from what I think, from what I have seen, from what I have analyzed and the conclusions that I have reached. It is not a case of being good or bad blacks and whites, it’s the case of being good or bad human beings.”_
---
[](https://www.kennedy24.com/donate?e=d33e868971601c1c714cfe0555abd394&utm_source=joinkennedy&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=malcom_x_2_29_24_rs_nd3&n=5)
---
Malcolm came to believe it was his purpose to unite people across racial lines to challenge the power of oppression and injustice in America. _I want to invoke his example today at a time of renewed hatred, polarization and division_.
It’s been the purpose of my campaign, to put aside the divisions and solve the real problems that afflict Americans of all skin colors.

Along with my uncle, my father, and Martin Luther King, it was one of four assassinations of the 1960s that devastated the soul of our nation. Malcolm’s death was especially tragic because it came at a moment where the arc of his life had swung toward viewing all people as part of the brotherhood of humanity. The central revelation that transformed him was a trip to Mecca where he saw people of every race, creed and color worshiping in the same places and praying to the same god. After that, he saw his life’s mission as being a truth teller: “I’m speaking now from what I think, from what I have seen, from what I have analyzed and the conclusions that I have reached. Final Sprint to the March 5th Primary | | | [](https://mgcp02.engage.squarespace-mail.com/r?m=65e08fdfa5c8b20a7a2f2a36&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.jobyforcongress.com%2F%3Fss_source%3Dsscampaigns%26ss_campaign_id%3D65dd2e49f568613fa4067cb3%26ss_email_id%3D65e08fdfa5c8b20a7a2f2a36%26ss_campaign_name%3DWe%2Bare%2Bmaking%2Bwaves.%2B%26ss_campaign_sent_date%3D2024-02-29T14%253A15%253A58Z&w=6514833727955b66bdb4f35b&c=b_65dd2e49f568613fa4067cb3&l=en-US&s=1mKIEQ48zD2LWuTRxKDvRYEWUv4%3D)
---
| Hi Friend -First off, wanted to share with you exciting recent headlines:
* **Inside Climate News** wrote an article about how our campaign is bringing climate to the forefront. Check it out [here](https://mgcp02.engage.squarespace-mail.com/r?m=65e08fdfa5c8b20a7a2f2a36&u=https%3A%2F%2Finsideclimatenews.org%2Fnews%2F28022024%2Fjoby-bernstein-california-primary%2F&w=6514833727955b66bdb4f35b&c=b_65dd2e49f568613fa4067cb3&l=en-US&s=34Kwysx2jcTTpAkWQFIaBX6C3gI%3D).
* Joby was a guest on one of our favorite podcasts (**Cherie’s Corner**). Podcast just dropped, watch it [here](https://mgcp02.engage.squarespace-mail.com/r?m=65e08fdfa5c8b20a7a2f2a36&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Findex%3D1%26list%3DPLmQIdka2UzDXCOYGXqNNCaj5HhwDpjW_A%26v%3DrfDi_KmXq6Q&w=6514833727955b66bdb4f35b&c=b_65dd2e49f568613fa4067cb3&l=en-US&s=VmRl8HXFjdAAPsq3S1FzllNkAOc%3D).
* On Thursday, Joby participated in a history-making candidate forum. The 16th District **Congressional District Primary**[**Forum**](https://mgcp02.engage.squarespace-mail.com/r?m=65e08fdfa5c8b20a7a2f2a36&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.linkedin.com%2Fposts%2Flosaltosinstitution_we-hope-you-can-join-us-for-this-historic-activity-7166097319799595010-erSW%3Futm_medium%3Dmember_ios%26utm_source%3Dshare&w=6514833727955b66bdb4f35b&c=b_65dd2e49f568613fa4067cb3&l=en-US&s=qBlDPYX0gluULpQE1VLNoVcFXjg%3D), hosted by the Los Altos Institution and Palo Alto High School's Associated Student Body, was the first ever debate hosted by high school students. Also, see coverage by [CBS News](https://mgcp02.engage.squarespace-mail.com/r?m=65e08fdfa5c8b20a7a2f2a36&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.cbsnews.com%2Fsanfrancisco%2Fnews%2Fsouth-bay-high-school-students-forum-congress-candidates%2F&w=6514833727955b66bdb4f35b&c=b_65dd2e49f568613fa4067cb3&l=en-US&s=lGJ_RAsr-GXSvGHvGYu0IxtG-sk%3D) and [Palo Alto Online](https://mgcp02.engage.squarespace-mail.com/r?m=65e08fdfa5c8b20a7a2f2a36&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.paloaltoonline.com%2Fregional-politics%2F2024%2F02%2F23%2Fcandidates-for-congress-make-their-case-at-youth-forum%2F&w=6514833727955b66bdb4f35b&c=b_65dd2e49f568613fa4067cb3&l=en-US&s=RIcQQRQqiS7bYdFtecIC31OMvbM%3D).
* On Sunday, Joby joined the final candidate debate in Half Moon Bay, hosted by the **Coastside Democratic Club**. You can watch the video [here](https://mgcp02.engage.squarespace-mail.com/r?m=65e08fdfa5c8b20a7a2f2a36&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3D7BJcDmsLA3A&w=6514833727955b66bdb4f35b&c=b_65dd2e49f568613fa4067cb3&l=en-US&s=KOKVVbFPEwjve26HmwiWUj36hcM%3D).

We are getting close to **1 million views** on our [YouTube Ads](https://mgcp02.engage.squarespace-mail.com/r?m=65e08fdfa5c8b20a7a2f2a36&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fchannel%2FUC7w5byEDhj6z7NxvcOSI7Hg&w=6514833727955b66bdb4f35b&c=b_65dd2e49f568613fa4067cb3&l=en-US&s=Wzfdz0Kr5RRKA9CEZzLy0JDo-5g%3D). If you don’t live in the district, and haven’t been seeing them, you can watch copies on our channel [here](https://mgcp02.engage.squarespace-mail.com/r?m=65e08fdfa5c8b20a7a2f2a36&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fchannel%2FUC7w5byEDhj6z7NxvcOSI7Hg&w=6514833727955b66bdb4f35b&c=b_65dd2e49f568613fa4067cb3&l=en-US&s=Wzfdz0Kr5RRKA9CEZzLy0JDo-5g%3D).It was another **busy week** on the campaign trail! Two debates, hikes, meet & greets, habitat restoration volunteering, and we knocked on over 1,500 doors! Saturday was an exciting day canvassing in Palo Alto - our biggest day of canvassing yet! On Sunday, we had an action-packed day at the coast. The day started with a beach hike and volunteering at Linda Mar Beach with the Pacifica Beach Coalition. We then headed to Half Moon Bay for a couple hours of canvassing, followed by the final candidate debate, hosted by the Coastside Democratic Club. **Ballots are out!** You have **5 DAYS** to vote and **CONVINCE YOUR FRIENDS TO VOTE FOR JOBY.****UPCOMING EVENTS** **GET INVOLVED! Our FINAL PRE-PRIMARY canvassing this weekend! **
* _**Saturday** , March 2 from 11-1pm_
* _**Sunday** , March 3 from 10:30am-1pm_
* _**Monday** **Lit Drop** , March 4 - any help is welcome! _**
**[**Sign up here!** ](https://mgcp02.engage.squarespace-mail.com/r?m=65e08fdfa5c8b20a7a2f2a36&u=https%3A%2F%2Fdocs.google.com%2Fspreadsheets%2Fd%2F1tQKrs2k8T1qzl93PMn6DQ69RaU8x_vx-wK_qocNpHzI%2Fedit%23gid%3D0&w=6514833727955b66bdb4f35b&c=b_65dd2e49f568613fa4067cb3&l=en-US&s=2QvLm1dvPVL09RONIlfeLVO_zTs%3D)

Free car shuttles from Stanford! Exact location will be sent to sign ups! **March with Joby!** _**Saturday, March 3 from 1:30-4:30pm**._ Unity March Against Antisemitism in San Francisco. For more info, email hello@jobyforcongress.com or visit https://www.unitymarch.ca/

subject: I'm writing to personally ask you to make a $3 contribution to our campaign before tonight's end-of-month fundraising deadline. Here's why:
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY ILHAN FOR CONGRESS
body:
This movement's support is something I will never take for granted.
# [](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/35?t=1&akid=977%2E791427%2EfDQGg_)

Friends -
The worst part about running for Congress is — without a doubt — the obscene amount of money it takes to build a successful campaign.
We all know that there is far, far too much money in our political system. But I also know that in order for our movement to be successful and win, we have to have the resources required to stay competitive.
That's especially true when the right wing and their super PACs target a campaign as directly as they do ours. They're preparing to spend unlimited sums of dark money on everything from bigoted ads to propping up my opponents to try and defeat us.
Meanwhile, we're doing things the right way — together. **That means I'm counting on lots and lots of people making lots and lots of small contributions to win this race.**
So I have to ask. We're facing an important monthly fundraising deadline at midnight tonight, and I'm hoping you can make your first contribution to stand with me before it ends.
What do you say?
**[Please add a contribution — $3 or any amount that works for you — before tonight's deadline. This campaign is funded by lots of people giving small amounts at a time, so every dollar makes a difference.](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/7?c0=io-em-feb24.LBKb43&refcode=em240229-1-t1&t=2&akid=977%2E791427%2EfDQGg_)**

body:
The choice is yours, but we hope that you’ll consider making a contribution to GIFFORDS PAC today
#

**January 8, 2013**
This was the day that Gabby Giffords founded Americans for Responsible Solutions, the organization now known as GIFFORDS. Since then, we’ve been working to elect gun safety champions up and down the ballot, help pass gun safety legislation nationwide, and organize a community of supporters who are all united behind the common cause of keeping our communities safe from gun violence.
**February 29, 2024**

No matter why you are reading this, I am thankful for you.
People like me don’t often make it to Congress.
I’m the son of Latino immigrants, who, with my three sisters, was raised by my single mother. I was the first in my family to attend college, cleaning the toilets of my classmates to make it work, and I joined the Marine Corps after graduating and went to Iraq.
The only reason I am here is because of the support I’ve had along the way.
As a kid, the support from my family.
In combat, the support of my fellow Marines.
In these campaigns, support from people like you.

Here’s the truth: No matter why you are reading this, I am thankful for you. People like me don’t often make it to Congress. I’m the son of Latino immigrants, who, with my three sisters, was raised by my single mother. I was the first in my family to attend college, cleaning the toilets of my classmates to make it work, and I joined the Marine Corps after graduating and went to Iraq. body:
“coup for the old-guard Democratic moderates”
# [](https://act.katieporter.com/go/14558?t=1&akid=38421%2E3422442%2E7myVHs)
Derek, I’m a straight-shooter, and right now that means telling you that with just 5 days until the election, **I’m at real risk of losing.** Anything you can give right now will be put to immediate use reaching voters.
**[Yes, I can give $5.](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/kp4s-em-20240229-1?refcode=em20240229-38421&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&refcode2=38421_3422442_7myVHs&akid=38421%2E3422442%2E7myVHs)**
Here’s the deal, recent polls show this race as a dead heat for second place. Second place really matters, because the top two primary finishers advance to the general.
Schiff is currently polling in first place, and because general election polls show I have a strong chance of winning in a head to head matchup, Schiff is spending millions of dollars to consolidate GOP support behind former LA Dodger, Steve Garvey. As Slate reported:
_"If Garvey does advance, it would essentially ensure that a centrist like Schiff would win the general election for the Senate seat—**a coup for the old-guard Democratic moderates like Nancy Pelosi, and a frustrating miss for progressives** hoping to shift Feinstein’s old seat at least slightly to the left."_
Derek, this race is not about me. It’s about the future of our country and of our party. Washington is broken, and the answer isn’t to send more of the same.
I’m a single mom of three school aged kids who first ran for office in 2018. I raised my hand to run because as a consumer protection advocate, I saw how corporate special interests were making it difficult for working people to get ahead.
I don’t look or talk like most other Members of Congress—and I don’t fundraise like them either. As the only candidate in this race who has never taken corporate PAC money and supports banning it altogether, I truly count on support from real people, $5 or $50 at a time.
This could be one of the last times I ask: **[Can you be the reason I stay in Congress fighting against corruption and corporate greed?](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/kp4s-em-20240229-1?refcode=em20240229-38421&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&refcode2=38421_3422442_7myVHs&akid=38421%2E3422442%2E7myVHs)**

Onward to Election Day,
Katie

subject: IVF ban: Death Eaters would be so proud.
body:
Trump is Voldemort who was fading away. The Press and The Democratic Party were Horcruxes that revived him, paving the way for a Death Eater Agenda. | | | | |
---
Two friends mentioned recently that they were not supporting Biden and were on the fence about Trump. I was speechless, but this week’s post contains what I wish I had said.
**[READ ME]**[ The Death Eater Power Play with Trump as Voldemort and Mike Johnson as Lucious Malfoy](https://substack.us8.list-manage.com/track/click?u=833a984b31aaa09af9ff0ffae&id=8f12cfa1b5&e=0f9388ee95)
My friends’ remarks came just as Republicans backed a bill that in all likelihood would block in vitro fertilization, the miracle that enabled my husband and I to have children. The 124 sponsors of the bill claim to be protecting life when they are in fact paving the way for so many millions to never experience the joy of bringing a new life into this world.
I struggled with both pieces of news and then realized how they are connected.
Trump is like a Floridian Voldemort from the Harry Potter books. His supporters in Congress are like Death Eaters. Their motivating force is cruelty.
Trump was, in fact, waning in popularity as of November 2022. Then Democrats started campaigning for the 2024 election. And Media started covering those campaigns. The Democratic Party and the Media unintentionally gave Trump the Horcrux of free advertising that called the Death Eaters to rise and brazenly attack women, children, immigrants, People of Color, Gay and Trans people, and those struggling financially.
**The 2024 Presidential Election is not about Biden versus Trump. It is about Humanity versus Inhumanity.** If I thought that before, the fact that I may never have been able to be a mother in a Trump / Death Eater world makes me 100% convinced of that now. Thanks for [reading this week’s post and subscribing to the newsletter](https://substack.us8.list-manage.com/track/click?u=833a984b31aaa09af9ff0ffae&id=0594f9f807&e=0f9388ee95).
Lexi

body:
# [](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/188?t=1&akid=1159%2E135344%2EiWWryi)

Friends --
Today is the last day of February, and that means if you're anything like us, your inbox is filled with requests from political campaigns and organizations asking for donations.
With your permission, I’d appreciate the chance to make the case for why a donation to my campaign for U.S. Senate is one of the most strategic contributions you can make before midnight.
Let me start with what you probably already instinctively know: Michigan is going to be a critical state for the 2024 campaign.
There is no winning the White House without Michigan. For Democrats, there is no holding the Senate without Michigan. Even our House delegation rests on a one-seat Democratic majority.
But you were probably already sold on the importance of Michigan. So, aside from the fact that control of the U.S. Senate is at stake (!), what about my race? Why donate to my campaign?
This is one of the rare open Senate races without an incumbent running – in fact, it’s the only competitive open seat in the entire country. That means we have A LOT of introducing of me to do across the state. A recent poll showed about 50% of the state knows me, across our 11 media markets.
Reaching those folks takes resources, and that's not something I can do without you.
Add the fact that this is going to be one of the most expensive races in the country -- not just with candidate spending, but outside spending too.
And I'll close with the news that in all of my elections, I have historically done better than Democrats usually do in the "redder" areas of the state. That means I am finding and pulling voters other races couldn't, and that is good for everyone up and down the ballot on Election Day.
So yes, this race is kind of a unicorn. It's a unique situation where control of the White House and Congress is on the line, most voters don't know the candidates yet, and the Democratic Senate candidate can help the top of the ticket, and not the other way around.
[**That's why I am asking for your support: Can I count on you to make a contribution to my campaign for U.S. Senate before our February fundraising drive ends at midnight tonight? I would not ask if it were not so important.](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/9?c0=ebs-em-feb24.z4X5uQ&refcode=em240229-1-700&t=2&akid=1159%2E135344%2EiWWryi)**

[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP13/1/87444/images/New%20Sewell%20Delegate%20Logo%20.png]
Session Week 7 Newsletter
Dear Neighbor,
On Sunday, February 18th, the Virginia House of Delegates and State Senate released their budget proposals, outlining priorities and focusing on critical areas. While there is broad agreement on areas in need of investment and a vision for a stronger, more vibrant, and prosperous Commonwealth there are significant differences that conferees from both chambers will hammer out in the coming weeks. You can take a look at the overview of the House budget amendments here [https://hac.virginia.gov/Committee/files/2024/2-18-24/2 - Budget Report Out Briefing.pdf] and the Senate budget amendments here [https://budget.lis.virginia.gov/sessionreports/2024/1/] , by clicking “Senate Finance & Appropriations Subcommittees.”
When the budget was introduced last week, Delegate Luke Torian, who chairs the House Appropriations Committee, delivered remarks about the House’s budget proposal. I am honored to serve alongside Delegate Torian on the Appropriations Committee as one of its newest members. I was proud to sign onto this historic budget last week and vote with 74 other members of the House of Delegates to pass the budget bill and send it to conference with the Senate. This budget includes record investments in child care and early childhood education, K-12 through higher education, transportation, Medicaid, and mental health.
Several of my budget amendments made it into the final budget, see below:
187#2h - UVA Hospital - Hologic 3D Mammography System - $500,000
This amendment seeks to expand access to high-quality mammograms to address disparities in mammography rates among Black and Hispanic women by expanding access to affordable mammograms where community members live and work, so that child care, time off work, and transportation can no longer get in the way of critical screenings for patients. This budget amendment will be used to update UVA Health’s mobile mammography technology to a Hologic 3D system in the counties of Prince William, Fauquier, Louisa, Orange, and Madison, the cities of Manassas and Manassas Park, and the towns of Culpeper and Haymarket. This new technology finds cancers earlier than 2D mammography machines increasing the likelihood of cancer detection by 27% and a 40% increase in invasive cancer detection.
275#1h - HB 732 Naloxone Distribution in Schools - $100,000
This amendment seeks to address the opioid epidemic by ensuring every school in the Commonwealth has the funding to store two doses of Naloxone, a life-saving medication, in case of an opioid overdose. The funding will enable the Department of Health to distribute a supply of opioid antagonists (Naloxone) to every public elementary and secondary school in the Commonwealth for the 2025-2026 school year so that school staff have the resources they need to save lives.
114#2h - 2024 Solheim Cup - $5,000,000
This amendment will help provide public safety and transportation services to the more than 150,000 spectators who will attend the Solheim Cup, the second most-watched women’s sporting event in the world. The six-day golf tournament between Team USA and Team Europe, which will be held at Robert Trent Jones Golf Club located in Gainesville in Prince William County, will generate an estimated economic impact of over $60 million to the Commonwealth of Virginia. Broadcast to over 21.3 million people across the globe, the tournament will utilize over $5 million in Virginia-based logistics and event contractors. This event will showcase our Commonwealth to the entire world to show that we are a destination for world-class sporting events! Learn more about the Solheim Cup by visiting https://www.solheimcupusa.com/ [https://www.solheimcupusa.com/] .
297#1h - Increase Funding for Permanent Supportive Housing - $5,000,000 each year
This amendment will expand permanent supportive housing (PSH) for individuals with serious mental illness, helping them avoid homelessness and needless hospitalization. This money will go a long way to address the need for an estimated 5,000 additional units of housing for these community members. Research has shown that PSH reduces the utilization of emergency, crisis, and institutional care and improves housing stability for highly vulnerable people. The lack of housing options is the most common barrier to state hospital discharge. By investing in more PSH, Virginia can reduce the length of hospital stays, save money, and greatly improve the quality of life for those living with serious mental illnesses.
How to learn more about the House Budget
You can read a summary of what Delegate Torian said about the budget here [https://hac.virginia.gov/Committee/files/2024/2-18-24/1 - Torian Remarks 2024 Report Out.pdf] . You can also find information about the different House Appropriations Subcommittee reports that helped inform the larger budget proposal here [https://hac.virginia.gov/] . Finally, if you would like to watch the full House Appropriations Committee meeting that was held on Sunday, there is a recording of the livestream available. Here are directions on how to access it:
(1) Visit the official House of Delegates Video Streaming page here. [https://virginiageneralassembly.gov/house/chamber/chamberstream.php]
(2) On the bottom left, you’ll see a calendar. Click on the date for Sunday, February 18th.
(3) That will take you to a separate page for all the Committee meetings held that day.
(4) Click on the “Appropriations [HAC12]” entry.
(5) That will take you to a new page. A video player will load. Press play on that screen, and you can watch the full Appropriations Committee meeting.
As voters, residents, and constituents, I think it is vitally important that you not only have access to this information, but your elected officials make it as easy as possible for you to access it. If you’re having trouble accessing any of the budget-related material, please email my office at DelBSewell@house.virginia.gov [DelBSewell@house.virginia.gov] .
Budget Breakdown
There are several items included in the House’s version of the budget on which I would like to provide more in-depth information. While every dollar spent in the final budget will impact individuals and families all across the Commonwealth, I want to highlight historic investments in early childhood education, childcare, public schools, mental health, Medicaid, and transportation.
Investing in Public Education
Increasing funding for our public schools, supporting teachers, providing more resources to some of our highest-need students, and helping build a K-12 system that puts our youngest Virginians on the path to success is essential. Our children deserve a world-class education, our families and advocates are calling for it, and the Commonwealth depends on it.
In our budget proposal, the House of Delegates:
Provides $2.56 billion total over the biennium in direct aid for both early childhood and K-12 education.
This includes $2.2 billion over the biennium specifically for K-12, providing funding for more reading specialists in grades 4-8, lower-income students, improving staffing ratios for English language learners, and other critical items.
The $2.2 billion includes $384.6 million to support at-risk students while also updating how the state identifies “at-risk” to better serve more students in need.
Provides $628.2 million for two 3 3/8% salary increases for teachers to get Virginia closer to the national average in teacher pay (local school divisions will be required to provide 2% of the funding to get the full amount from the state).
Provides $418.1 million to expand Virginia’s early childhood system without increasing the copays families have to cover.
Provides $4.4 million to train special education teachers on inclusivity practices and establish regional parent support centers
Directs the Department of Education to enter into a statewide contract with a telehealth provider to allow school divisions to purchase mental health services for students
Child Care
Child care is an essential prerequisite for families to thrive in their jobs and communities. I am proud that this budget includes some much-needed investments that help protect our program and investments that face a federal fiscal cliff as pandemic funding dries up. See a brief description of these investments from the subcommittee report below.
“Finally, for our littlest learners, Virginia was in danger of losing about 35,000 – roughly half - of the funded early childhood slots available for lower-income families as federal funding will soon disappear. As such, I am proud to present a $418.1 million plan that will ensure those slots are maintained and even provide some room for expansion, all without increasing the financial burden on working families. Within this plan, we also propose an innovative public-private partnership to provide up to a 25 percent state match for employers willing to share in the cost of child care within their workforce.”
This is a snapshot of the education portion of the House’s proposed two-year budget. You can find more specifics in the Appropriation Committee presentations here [https://hac.virginia.gov/Committee/files/2024/2-18-24/2 - Budget Report Out Briefing.pdf] and here [https://hac.virginia.gov/Committee/files/2024/2-18-24/3 - Elem & Sec Ed Report.pdf] .
Transportation Investments:
Metro and Potomac Rappahannock Transportation Commission (PRTC)
Public transportation in Prince William County and across Northern Virginia is always a pressing issue because of the essential role it plays in our regional connectivity and economic stability. Our NoVA transportation networks don’t just impact Northern Virginia; they have a dramatic impact on Virginia as a whole and require our support to make sure this critical part of our transportation infrastructure is successful, sustainable, and adaptable. The House’s proposed budget understands this reality and makes some significant investments accordingly.
In our budget proposal, the House of Delegates:
Provides $149.5 million over two years in increased funding for the Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority (WMATA). This will help address the financial shortfall WMATA is facing, driven largely by COVID and the increase in teleworking.
Establishes a Joint Subcommittee to study funding, cost controls, and strategies to ensure all Northern Virginia transit systems, including the Metro and the Potomac Rappahannock Transportation Commission (PRTC) [https://www.spotsylvania.va.us/1303/Potomac-and-Rappahannock-Transportation-] , can meet growing needs.
Established a working group consisting of area transit systems, including the PRTC, to further examine additional revenue sources.
The working group may also propose more revenue sources that could contribute to funding Northern Virginia transit agencies, in addition to current state and local funding.
You can read the full House Appropriations Transportation Subcommittee report here [https://hac.virginia.gov/Committee/files/2024/2-18-24/9 - Transportation & Public Safety Report.pdf] .
Medicaid and Mental Health Care
Virginians are facing a mental health care crisis. Access to quality health care when it is needed and without delay can be the key component to keeping families thriving together when a mental and physical health crisis arises. The budget includes critical investments in quality care that people can access when they need it most. Key investments include:
$457 million over the biennium to support behavioral health and substance use disorder services.
$55 million is dedicated to crisis services to provide immediate support to individuals who need it most.
$12 million for discharge assistance planning for patients on the extraordinary barriers list.
$30 million to develop school-based health centers to provide mental health and primary medical care to students and their families within the school.
Funding to fully clear the 3,440 Priority 1 waiver slots over the biennium -- 1,720 slots each year, with provisions to ensure providers can absorb this additional demand, through increased reimbursement rates and phased-in slots.
$125.0 million as a reserve for increased Medicaid expenditures.
$81.6 million for value-based nursing home payments.
$7.0 million for community health care centers and free clinics.
$6.4 million to continue funding community health workers in our local health districts.
$6.5 million for brain injury services and workforce retention efforts for service providers.
You can read more about Medicaid, and mental and behavioral health care investments in this budget through the subcommittee report here [https://hac.virginia.gov/Committee/files/2024/2-18-24/4 - Health & Human Resources Report.pdf] .
A House of Delegates Tradition
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP13/1/87444/images/Screenshot%202024-02-29%20at%209.00.56%20AM.png]
The tradition of opening the House of Delegates with an invocation from a religious leader dates back to the beginnings of the House of Delegates. On Thursday, February 22nd, Rabbi Lizz Goldstein of Congregation Ner Shalom [https://www.nershalomva.org/] visited Richmond to deliver the Invocation to open the House of Delegates floor session for the day. You can watch Rabbi Goldstein’s opening invocation here [https://virginiageneralassembly.gov/house/chamber/chamberstream.php] by clicking on the date (February 22nd) and selecting "Regular Session (House Chamber)."
If you know of a member of our Prince William religious community who might want the opportunity to offer the House opening invocation, please feel free to reach out to our office, and we will try to coordinate a visit. Prayers must be ecumenical and welcoming to all, and Delegates are asked to reach out to religious leaders in their community to invite them down to Richmond to offer the opening invocation. You can learn more about the history of religious freedom in Virginia here [https://www.monticello.org/research-education/thomas-jefferson-encyclopedia/virginia-statute-religious-freedom/] and the invocation in the House of Delegates here [https://www.wtvr.com/2017/05/04/general-assembly-prayer] .
Welcome to Richmond! Constituent Engagement and More
I appreciate everyone who visited me in Richmond this week to provide their input or feedback on legislation, update me on their organization, or just to say hello.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP13/1/87444/images/IMG_0523.jpg] I met with representatives from the Medical Society of Virginia [https://www.msv.org/] . We discussed the needs of physicians and practitioners across the Commonwealth.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP13/1/87444/images/IMG_0549.jpg] I welcomed the Prince William County Girl Scouts Troop 18022 [https://www.pwcva.gov/department/childrens-programs/scouting] to Richmond. They toured the capitol, watched the Appropriations Committee in action, and learned more about the importance of state and local leadership.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP13/1/87444/images/IMG_0530.jpg] The advocacy organization Fund Our Schools [https://www.fundourschoolsva.org/] stopped by my office where we discussed the need for the General Assembly to fully fund our public education system and support our students.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP13/1/87444/images/IMG_0535.jpg] I was happy to meet with the Osbourn Park High School Robotics Team, known as the Metal Jackets [https://www.metaljackets.org/] . It was great hearing from these impressive students, who represent the next generation of engineers and technology leaders.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP13/1/87444/images/IMG_0580.jpg] Virginia Tech’s [https://www.vt.edu/] Hokie Day took place this week, and my legislative assistant, Jay, was able to meet with some of my constituents to discuss the contributions of Virginia Tech and ongoing state support for this institution.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP13/1/87444/images/IMG_0525.jpg] My legislative assistant, Jay, met with representatives from RISE for Youth [https://www.riseforyouth.org/] to hear about their ongoing efforts to divert youth from the criminal justice system and support communities in need.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP13/1/87444/images/IMG_0527.jpg] Finally, Jay met with Red, Wine, and Blue [https://redwine.blue/] to discuss their continued advocacy for public education and the need to push back against growing extremism on local school boards.
Bills
My bills are moving through the Senate. Check out their progress below:
HB738 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?ses=241&typ=bil&val=HB738+] ensures all members of the armed forces have access to the same earned benefits no matter their service branch. This bill was sent to the Senate floor on February 16th and passed the Senate unanimously 39-0 on February 19th.
HB739 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?ses=241&typ=bil&val=HB739+] attempts to address the military child care provider crisis by exempting from duplicative Virginia licensure DOD-licensed family providers that are based on military installations or serve only military families. This bill was sent to the Senate floor on February 16th and passed the Senate unanimously 39-0 on February 19th.
HB1526 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?ses=241&typ=bil&val=HB1526] allows the DMV to issue overweight permits for an electric utility's operation of vehicles to allow more efficient uses of utility crews and vehicles and ensure power is returned more quickly during outages. This bill was sent to the Senate floor on February 16th and passed the Senate unanimously 40-0 on February 20th.
HB731 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?ses=241&typ=bil&val=HB731+] works to fix the leaky teacher pipeline and increase teacher diversity through the elimination of a duplicative, expensive, and out-of-date testing requirement for teachers. This bill passed the Senate Education Subcommittee on Public Education unanimously, 5 - 0, on February 22nd.
HB732 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?ses=241&typ=bil&val=HB732] requires schools to stock and train staff on the administration of Naloxone, a life-saving medication, in case of an opioid overdose. This bill passed the Senate Education Subcommittee on Public Education unanimously, 5 - 0, on February 22nd.
HB736 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?ses=241&typ=bil&val=HB736] : protects veterans from predatory Veterans Affairs benefits claim sharks. This bill was heard by the Senate Commerce and Labor Committee on Monday.
Subcommittees
Two of the three subcommittees that I chair met, and these are the actions we took on legislation that was sent to us from the Senate. Click on the title of the subcommittee below to watch the recording of the public hearing on each bill.
Counties, Cities, and Towns Subcommittee #2 [https://virginiageneralassembly.gov/house/chamber/chamberstream.php] :
SB17 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?ses=241&typ=bil&val=SB17] : passed the bill
SB316 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?ses=241&typ=bil&val=SB316] : passed the bill
SB304 [https://virginiageneralassembly.gov/house/chamber/chamberstream.php] : passed by for the day
Higher Education Subcommittee [https://virginiageneralassembly.gov/house/chamber/chamberstream.php] :
SB21 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?ses=241&typ=bil&val=SB21] : passed the bill with a substitute
SB420 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?ses=241&typ=bil&val=SB420] : passed the bill with amendments
SB506 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?ses=241&typ=bil&val=SB506] : passed the bill with a substitute, referred the bill to the Appropriations Committee
This Week’s Mailbag
As we engage in important budget discussions and continue to consider legislation from the Senate, my team and I appreciate your ongoing outreach and willingness to provide feedback about specific bills.
This week, we’ve heard about legislation related to requirements for realtors and consumer protections, calls for protections for LGBTQ+ Virginians, and inquiries about supporting additional environmental protections.
If you have ideas, thoughts, or concerns about legislation being considered by the House or questions about the budget process, please do not hesitate to reach out at DelBSewell@house.virginia.gov [DelBSewell@house.virginia.gov] .
Stay In Touch!
While we’ve passed the halfway point of the General Assembly Session, a lot of work remains, including finalizing a budget. As our work continues, I want to thank you for your continued engagement, and I look forward to hearing from you as the session continues through February and into early March.
Remember, you can always reach out to my office with questions or concerns. Send me an email at DelBSewell@house.virginia.gov [DelBSewell@house.virginia.gov] , call our Richmond office at 703-261-4787, or visit us in person at 201 North 9th Street, Suite 905, Richmond, VA 23219.
Take care, have a great weekend, and I look forward to appearing in your inboxes next week with more updates from Richmond!

Establishes a Joint Subcommittee to study funding, cost controls, and strategies to ensure all Northern Virginia transit systems, including the Metro and the Potomac Rappahannock Transportation Commission (PRTC) [-] , can meet growing needs. Established a working group consisting of area transit systems, including the PRTC, to further examine additional revenue sources. The working group may also propose more revenue sources that could contribute to funding Northern Virginia transit agencies, in addition to current state and local funding. You can read the full House Appropriations Transportation Subcommittee report here [ - Transportation & Public Safety Report.pdf] . Medicaid and Mental Health Care Virginians are facing a mental health care crisis. Access to quality health care when it is needed and without delay can be the key component to keeping families thriving together when a mental and physical health crisis arises. The budget includes critical investments in quality care that people can access when they need it most. Key investments include: $457 million over the biennium to support behavioral health and substance use disorder services. $55 million is dedicated to crisis services to provide immediate support to individuals who need it most. $12 million for discharge assistance planning for patients on the extraordinary barriers list. $30 million to develop school-based health centers to provide mental health and primary medical care to students and their families within the school. Funding to fully clear the 3,440 Priority 1 waiver slots over the biennium -- 1,720 slots each year, with provisions to ensure providers can absorb this additional demand, through increased reimbursement rates and phased-in slots. $125.0 million as a reserve for increased Medicaid expenditures. $81.6 million for value-based nursing home payments. $7.0 million for community health care centers and free clinics. $6.4 million to continue funding community health workers in our local health districts. $6.5 million for brain injury services and workforce retention efforts for service providers. You can read more about Medicaid, and mental and behavioral health care investments in this budget through the subcommittee report here [ - Health & Human Resources Report.pdf] . A House of Delegates Tradition [] The tradition of opening the House of Delegates with an invocation from a religious leader dates back to the beginnings of the House of Delegates. On Thursday, February 22nd, Rabbi Lizz Goldstein of Congregation Ner Shalom [] visited Richmond to deliver the Invocation to open the House of Delegates floor session for the day. You can watch Rabbi Goldstein’s opening invocation here [] by clicking on the date (February 22nd) and selecting "Regular Session (House Chamber)." If you know of a member of our Prince William religious community who might want the opportunity to offer the House opening invocation, please feel free to reach out to our office, and we will try to coordinate a visit. Prayers must be ecumenical and welcoming to all, and Delegates are asked to reach out to religious leaders in their community to invite them down to Richmond to offer the opening invocation. You can learn more about the history of religious freedom in Virginia here [] and the invocation in the House of Delegates here [] . Welcome to Richmond! Constituent Engagement and More I appreciate everyone who visited me in Richmond this week to provide their input or feedback on legislation, update me on their organization, or just to say hello. [] I met with representatives from the Medical Society of Virginia [] . We discussed the needs of physicians and practitioners across the Commonwealth. [] I welcomed the Prince William County Girl Scouts Troop 18022 [] to Richmond. They toured the capitol, watched the Appropriations Committee in action, and learned more about the importance of state and local leadership. [] The advocacy organization Fund Our Schools [] stopped by my office where we discussed the need for the General Assembly to fully fund our public education system and support our students. [] I was happy to meet with the Osbourn Park High School Robotics Team, known as the Metal Jackets [] . It was great hearing from these impressive students, who represent the next generation of engineers and technology leaders. [] Virginia Tech’s [] Hokie Day took place this week, and my legislative assistant, Jay, was able to meet with some of my constituents to discuss the contributions of Virginia Tech and ongoing state support for this institution. [] My legislative assistant, Jay, met with representatives from RISE for Youth [] to hear about their ongoing efforts to divert youth from the criminal justice system and support communities in need. [] Finally, Jay met with Red, Wine, and Blue [] to discuss their continued advocacy for public education and the need to push back against growing extremism on local school boards. Bills My bills are moving through the Senate. Check out their progress below: HB738 [+] ensures all members of the armed forces have access to the same earned benefits no matter their service branch. This bill was sent to the Senate floor on February 16th and passed the Senate unanimously 39-0 on February 19th. HB739 [+] attempts to address the military child care provider crisis by exempting from duplicative Virginia licensure DOD-licensed family providers that are based on military installations or serve only military families. This bill was sent to the Senate floor on February 16th and passed the Senate unanimously 39-0 on February 19th. HB1526 [] allows the DMV to issue overweight permits for an electric utility's operation of vehicles to allow more efficient uses of utility crews and vehicles and ensure power is returned more quickly during outages. This bill was sent to the Senate floor on February 16th and passed the Senate unanimously 40-0 on February 20th. HB731 [+] works to fix the leaky teacher pipeline and increase teacher diversity through the elimination of a duplicative, expensive, and out-of-date testing requirement for teachers. This bill passed the Senate Education Subcommittee on Public Education unanimously, 5 - 0, on February 22nd. HB732 [] requires schools to stock and train staff on the administration of Naloxone, a life-saving medication, in case of an opioid overdose. This bill passed the Senate Education Subcommittee on Public Education unanimously, 5 - 0, on February 22nd. HB736 [] : protects veterans from predatory Veterans Affairs benefits claim sharks. This bill was heard by the Senate Commerce and Labor Committee on Monday. Subcommittees Two of the three subcommittees that I chair met, and these are the actions we took on legislation that was sent to us from the Senate. Click on the title of the subcommittee below to watch the recording of the public hearing on each bill. Counties, Cities, and Towns Subcommittee #2 [] : SB17 [] : passed the bill SB316 [] : passed the bill SB304 [] : passed by for the day Higher Education Subcommittee [] : SB21 [] : passed the bill with a substitute SB420 [] : passed the bill with amendments SB506 [] : passed the bill with a substitute, referred the bill to the Appropriations Committee This Week’s Mailbag As we engage in important budget discussions and continue to consider legislation from the Senate, my team and I appreciate your ongoing outreach and willingness to provide feedback about specific bills. This week, we’ve heard about legislation related to requirements for realtors and consumer protections, calls for protections for LGBTQ+ Virginians, and inquiries about supporting additional environmental protections. If you have ideas, thoughts, or concerns about legislation being considered by the House or questions about the budget process, please do not hesitate to reach out at DelBSewell@house.virginia.gov [DelBSewell@house.virginia.gov] . Stay In Touch! While we’ve passed the halfway point of the General Assembly Session, a lot of work remains, including finalizing a budget. As our work continues, I want to thank you for your continued engagement, and I look forward to hearing from you as the session continues through February and into early March. Remember, you can always reach out to my office with questions or concerns. Send me an email at DelBSewell@house.virginia.gov [DelBSewell@house.virginia.gov] , call our Richmond office at 703-261-4787, or visit us in person at 201 North 9th Street, Suite 905, Richmond, VA 23219. Take care, have a great weekend, and I look forward to appearing in your inboxes next week with more updates from Richmond! [] Paid for by Friends of Briana Sewell. Sarah Longwell

body:
#
[**Friend, I am respectfully asking you to contribute $3 before the Long Run’s February end-of-month fundraising deadline at midnight tonight.**](https://act.mandelabarnes.com/go/1212?c0=longrunpac-em-feb24.ocq2fh&refcode=em240229-1-tt&t=1&akid=5228%2E196590%2EkdnJar)
Here's why:
Over the past few years, Republican disarray has been on full display. Political challenges ranging from potential government shutdowns to chaotic leadership turnover in the House to sham impeachment attempts have made it crystal clear that Democrats _must_ win every seat they can in 2024.
We are facing Trump’s mega-donor-funded presidential campaign, a slim Democratic Senate majority, and a House filled with extremists that will do everything to further their agenda.
Make no mistake: our democracy is vulnerable.

[](https://click.everyaction.com/k/79984051/458100749/-2040236497?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9BVi9BVkxDVi8xLzcwODc3IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjI3MDczMzk3LTFiZDctZWUxMS04NWY5LTAwMjI0ODIyMzc5NCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=YRFuTKUZKDDmE-dJS1nCDuGeTcDzb0RvsCopOeCL5M4=&emci=dfca51a4-87d6-ee11-85f9-002248223794&emdi=27073397-1bd7-ee11-85f9-002248223794&ceid=2107230) | | | Dear Peter, Exciting update on the Right to Repair Act: it has passed the Senate and will now move on to the House for a vote! This is one of our top priority bills for the 2024 legislative session, so we need your help making sure it passes the House as well. [**Will you urge your Representative to vote YES on the Right to Repair Act (SB 1596)?**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/79984052/458100751/-2040236497?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9BVi9BVkxDVi8xLzcwODc3IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjI3MDczMzk3LTFiZDctZWUxMS04NWY5LTAwMjI0ODIyMzc5NCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=YRFuTKUZKDDmE-dJS1nCDuGeTcDzb0RvsCopOeCL5M4=&emci=dfca51a4-87d6-ee11-85f9-002248223794&emdi=27073397-1bd7-ee11-85f9-002248223794&ceid=2107230) The Right to Repair Act would give us the freedom to choose to repair our products ourselves or take them to third party repair shops, all by requiring manufacturing companies to make the required information, tools, and software available for consumers to fix their items. This will be much like how we repair cars, and the result will:
* Save families money
* Reduce e-waste
* Cut pollution

body:
|
# [](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/61?t=1&akid=5769%2E5257348%2EhDVvYA)
Derek — Today is a very special day for our family: It’s my father’s 96th birthday (Or 24th birthday if you only count the leap years!)
[**Will you help my family celebrate his birthday by signing his birthday card and adding your well wishes? It would mean so much to him — and I’ll explain why below.**](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/1024?c0=engagement-0229-Boca-Eddie-birthday-card.0xQz7H&refcode=AU_ABS_EG_GEN_GEN_AC90_20240229_AM1_V1_S1&email=&t=4&akid=5769%2E5257348%2EhDVvYA)
[SIGN THE CARD](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/1024?c0=engagement-0229-Boca-Eddie-birthday-card.0xQz7H&refcode=AU_ABS_EG_GEN_GEN_AC90_20240229_AM1_V1_S1&email=&t=5&akid=5769%2E5257348%2EhDVvYA)
---
My father, Ed — or as he’s known to many, Boca Eddie — taught me so many lessons while growing up. A proud veteran who left high school early to join the army at the end of WWII, he taught his two sons to respect those in uniform and to love our country. Here we are together at the WWII Memorial on the National Mall.
[](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/1024?c0=engagement-0229-Boca-Eddie-birthday-card.0xQz7H&refcode=AU_ABS_EG_GEN_GEN_AC90_20240229_AM1_V1_S1&email=&t=6&akid=5769%2E5257348%2EhDVvYA)
As kids, we moved around a lot for his work. From Massachusetts to Arizona, ending up in the Bay Area when I was eleven. Through it all, my parents worked hard to make sure my brother Dan and I had good neighborhoods to live in and good public schools to attend.
Even when times were tough — and there were times he said we all needed to tighten our belts — he made sure we gave back to others in our community.
You see, public service and giving back were important values in our household.
My parents believed in doing good for your community, being compassionate to everyone, and extending a helping hand to anyone needing one.
Those lessons have resonated with me in my work to this day. They have led me to pursue criminal justice reform, to make housing the homeless a top priority, to attack discrimination head-on, and to ensure the rule of law is applied justly.
**I am who I am today because of my parents, and I know he’s proud of the work I am doing each day to protect our democracy and make the world a better place.**
And oh yeah, it won’t surprise you to know that he doesn’t think much of Donald Trump. Without putting too fine a point on it — he thinks the man is a putz.
Another thing to know about my dad is that he calls it like it is. In fact, I remember telling him many years ago — when he turned 80 and was campaigning for Obama in Florida — that he had earned the right to speak his peace and not give a rat's ass if people didn’t like it. He assured me that he hadn’t waited until 80 to feel that way. So you can imagine how he is at 96!
[**So to bring an extra big smile to his face on his 96th birthday, will you sign his birthday card today?**](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/1024?c0=engagement-0229-Boca-Eddie-birthday-card.0xQz7H&refcode=AU_ABS_EG_GEN_GEN_AC90_20240229_AM1_V1_S1&email=&t=7&akid=5769%2E5257348%2EhDVvYA)
[SIGN THE CARD](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/1024?c0=engagement-0229-Boca-Eddie-birthday-card.0xQz7H&refcode=AU_ABS_EG_GEN_GEN_AC90_20240229_AM1_V1_S1&email=&t=8&akid=5769%2E5257348%2EhDVvYA)
---
Thank you, Derek. I wouldn’t be who I am today without my father, and I want to make sure he has a great day.
— Adam

clean_body: | Derek — Today is a very special day for our family: It’s my father’s 96th birthday (Or 24th birthday if you only count the leap years!) My father, Ed — or as he’s known to many, Boca Eddie — taught me so many lessons while growing up. A proud veteran who left high school early to join the army at the end of WWII, he taught his two sons to respect those in uniform and to love our country. Here we are together at the WWII Memorial on the National Mall. As kids, we moved around a lot for his work. From Massachusetts to Arizona, ending up in the Bay Area when I was eleven. Through it all, my parents worked hard to make sure my brother Dan and I had good neighborhoods to live in and good public schools to attend. Even when times were tough — and there were times he said we all needed to tighten our belts — he made sure we gave back to others in our community. You see, public service and giving back were important values in our household. My parents believed in doing good for your community, being compassionate to everyone, and extending a helping hand to anyone needing one. Those lessons have resonated with me in my work to this day. They have led me to pursue criminal justice reform, to make housing the homeless a top priority, to attack discrimination head-on, and to ensure the rule of law is applied justly. I am who I am today because of my parents, and I know he’s proud of the work I am doing each day to protect our democracy and make the world a better place. And oh yeah, it won’t surprise you to know that he doesn’t think much of Donald Trump. Without putting too fine a point on it — he thinks the man is a putz. Another thing to know about my dad is that he calls it like it is. In fact, I remember telling him many years ago — when he turned 80 and was campaigning for Obama in Florida — that he had earned the right to speak his peace and not give a rat's ass if people didn’t like it. He assured me that he hadn’t waited until 80 to feel that way. So you can imagine how he is at 96! Thank you, Derek. I wouldn’t be who I am today without my father, and I want to make sure he has a great day. — Adam | | 135 E. name: Nichole Johnson
subject: Peter, we had to make a difficult decision
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Gallego for Arizona
body:
We know outside groups are lining up against Ruben — from the National Republican Senatorial Committee to the MAGA-right extremist groups backing Trump.
#

Peter, it’s Nichole, Ruben Gallego’s Campaign Manager.
Tonight’s deadline is important, and not just because we’ve got to hit our goals. It’s likely the last deadline before Senator Sinema decides whether to run for re-election.
And before tonight’s deadline, before Senator Sinema makes her decision, we had to make a difficult decision of our own. I need you to hear about it:
We know outside groups are lining up against Ruben — from the National Republican Senatorial Committee to the MAGA-right extremist groups backing Trump.
We know they’re ready to do whatever it takes to take back this seat, and to expect millions of dollars in attack ads to drop at any time.
And we know that after Senator Sinema makes her decision, this race is going to change in a big way.
There were some critical investments we needed to make to be prepared for each of these scenarios, but our fundraising slowed down quite a bit over the last few weeks. We had to push off the decision to make those investments, but we couldn’t wait any longer...
So, I gave the green light. We’re doing it, even though the money wasn’t in the budget yet.
It was a difficult decision, but Ruben and I both know we’ve got an incredible team here. We’re banking on the fact that telling you all of this will convince you to chip in and help us fill that budget gap.
But the next part is up to you. We’re really counting on you here, so please:
[**Can you make a donation to Ruben’s campaign today, and help us close that budget gap before our deadline at midnight tonight? We’ll put every dollar right to work.**](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/1000?c0=ruben-em-feb24.Oewwi1&refcode=em240229-1-120&t=1&akid=2005%2E734936%2EFMuvSz)
[CONTRIBUTE](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/1000?c0=ruben-em-feb24.Oewwi1&refcode=em240229-1-120&t=2&akid=2005%2E734936%2EFMuvSz)
Thanks in advance for chipping in today. If there’s one thing that sets our campaign apart from everyone else in this race, it’s supporters like you.
You’re keeping us in the fight, and we won’t ever forget that.
Nichole

name: Justin Amash
subject: It's official: I'm running for U.S. Senate in Michigan
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY JUSTIN AMASH FOR SENATE
body:
| | [](https://connect.justinamash.com/r?u=vrqmj57zFGQGQEG7EgZ9L5rd8hHMjzS9pBGKcehw8LU&e=3ebc65ae19a1c85b4d26eca84f9aae52&utm_source=justinamash&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=announcement&n=1)
---
| Friend, When I established an exploratory committee for Senate, I understood the challenge ahead. Running for office requires an extraordinary commitment, not just from the candidate but also from family, friends, volunteers, and donors. A campaign puts them through so much. That’s reason enough not to run for office unless there’s a clear path to victory and a high likelihood of success. After thoroughly evaluating all aspects of a potential campaign, I’m convinced that no candidate would be better positioned to win both the Republican primary and the general election. That’s why, today, I’m making it official: I’m joining the race for United States Senate in Michigan. The past few years away from Congress have given me time to reflect on the experiences that have shaped my life, the principles of liberty that inspire me, and what my tenure in Congress meant to the people of my community. My parents arrived in the United States as teenagers in search of a better future—my father, a Palestinian refugee, and my mother, a Syrian immigrant. They instilled in me a love for America and for the values and principles at the heart of our Declaration of Independence and Constitution. We live in the greatest country on earth, but the ideals that have made it great are increasingly taken for granted. People often feel helpless and hopeless, unheard and ignored by Washington, and trapped between opposing forces who reject America’s principles or don’t understand them. So many times in my daily life, I’ve been approached by individuals who want me to know how much it meant to them that I did exactly what I said I’d do: that I upheld the Constitution regardless of the political consequences, that I read the bills, that I explained my votes, that I listened to the people I represented and held myself accountable to them in open town halls—giving them an opportunity to change my mind whenever we disagreed, and me an opportunity to change theirs. I feel an obligation to get back to this work, but the circumstances of this upcoming election give it urgency. Regardless of who wins the White House and Congress, the United States will remain deeply polarized. What we need is not a rubber stamp for either party, but an independent-minded senator prepared to challenge anyone and everyone on the people’s behalf—someone focused not on extending federal power so Republicans or Democrats in Washington can achieve their political ends, but on ensuring that Americans have the personal and economic freedom to pursue their own ends. As I wrote when I launched my exploratory committee: We need a principled, consistent constitutional conservative in the Senate—someone with a record of taking on the bipartisan oligarchy, defending sound money and free speech, fighting the surveillance state and military-industrial complex, and protecting all our rights. The advantage is ours in this battle, but that doesn’t mean victory will be easy. Mitch McConnell’s handpicked candidate, Mike Rogers, has built his career on expanding the power of the state at the expense of individual liberty, and the establishment will stop at nothing to get him elected. But I’d take you over them any day. Your financial support will be critical in this contest, so please give whatever you can at [justinamash.com](https://connect.justinamash.com/r?u=nPFaTKas50gnV2FjfYL96v0dKWFk77RJAQHLTjjwXLk&e=3ebc65ae19a1c85b4d26eca84f9aae52&utm_source=justinamash&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=announcement&n=2). These resources will support our operation to collect petition signatures to make the ballot and will allow us to build out our team across the state. Please also sign up at our website to let me know how you can contribute your time and talents to this effort. I’ll need your constant advocacy over the next several months. Videos, memes, graphics, messages—anything you can do to get the word out—will make a big difference. This is the land of liberty, and it’s on us to defend it. Thank you for standing with me. Justin Amash

clean_body: Trump and Biden are both visiting the border. | | | What do Joe Biden and Donald Trump have in common? Usually not a lot, buttoday, both will visit the southern border. Trump is visiting in support of Governor Greg Abbott and his inhumane decision to keep up razor wires and buoys along the border that put migrants in danger, despite direct orders from the Supreme Court to have them removed. Biden is visiting to make a call for additional border security, in the hopes that going after immigrants will win him more support in November. The border promises to be a hot-button issue for the rest of the election year, but both Biden and Trump’s political stunts are bound to draw attention away from actual solutions. Migrants are being put in physical danger every day while these men use them as scapegoats to advance in the polls. It’s disgusting, but not all that surprising. That’s why UWDA exists — to demand more of our politicians and pressure our government to produce actual solutions. subject: Charging debt on OUR credit card! 💳
body:
And my opponent celebrated it! |
---
| | Peter, I know I don't have to tell you how dire our country's fiscal situation is.

It got far worse last summer when career politicians in both parties voted to suspend the debt ceiling for two years without _any_ serious spending cuts.

_The result? They racked up $1 trillion in debt in just three weeks on OUR credit card!_

I saw that vote for what it was: another cowardly Washington failure. Another can kicked down the road.

[**But did you know that my opponent Scott Baugh _celebrated_ it?**](https://maxforoc.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=0d5d4fbfb4ace920581f6c90d&id=3dcb047002&e=86e91e802d)
---
| [ ](https://maxforoc.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=0d5d4fbfb4ace920581f6c90d&id=528dc57e4b&e=86e91e802d)
---
| Career politicians continue to screw us over again and again with reckless spending and skyrocketing inflation!

They got us into the mess. We need NEW leaders who will fight for bold action to get us out of it!

That’s why I’m running for Congress in the 47th District. I am a business owner, a political outsider, a conservative, and an America First patriot running to bring NEW leadership to Orange County.

Election Day is just five days away. I'm asking every patriot in Orange County for just TWO things:

1️⃣ Mail in your ballot and vote for MAX UKROPINA in the upcoming March 5 Primary Election!

2️⃣ [**Add your name and submit your official endorsement of my campaign for Congress! **](https://maxforoc.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=0d5d4fbfb4ace920581f6c90d&id=279d5852f0&e=86e91e802d)
---

---
| The fight to right to cut spending and right our fiscal ship won't be easy. But we'll never get it done if we don't fight and try.

I believe that fight is worth having because our country's future is worth fighting for.

[**If you're standing with me, I need your official endorsement TODAY.**](https://maxforoc.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=0d5d4fbfb4ace920581f6c90d&id=e5507756c3&e=86e91e802d)

I hope I can earn your vote on March 5!

Max Ukropina

Hi Derek, it’s John. I really need to talk to you about my friend Bob Casey.

Republicans are zeroing in on battleground states as we speak. Shady GOP PACs are already spending million$ to flip PA. There might be hundreds of times more money coming soon. 😨
**But I know we have what it takes to fight back and win.** By bringing together a grassroots team that can stand up to anything, we’ll keep making progress in our Commonwealth.
Together, we’ll defend PA’s Senate seat, as long as we don’t lose sight of the stakes. 💪 **Holding this seat is make-or-break for our Democratic majority.**
**[With that in mind... please, Derek, split a donation of $5 between our campaign + Bob Casey before the end-of-month deadline at MIDNIGHT so we can keep PA blue.](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jf-email-20240229-1?refcode=em20240229-1-8813&refcode2=8813_434096_KcNJou&akid=8813%2E434096%2EKcNJou)**

body:
Where John James stands on the issue | |
---
| | [ ](https://milwaukeedems.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e61dc0cbc36b6b9ece6e4cb38&id=5ea0698122&e=4d37f34e0f)
---
| | Hi Peter, Team Emily Busch here, and we wanted to make sure you heard:
_**Earlier this week, a ruling by the Alabama Supreme Court put the future of IVF in danger. **_
This effort joins a laundry list of initiatives led by Republicans to attack a person's right to reproductive care – abortion, contraception, and more.

Now more than ever, we need elected officials in Congress who understand that family planning decisions should be in the hands of the people, not politicians. Unfortunately, MI-10's own John James doesn't measure up.

**FIRST:** He said it himself – he is _**"100% pro life. Always have been, always will be."**_

**NEXT:** He voted against the Women's Protection Act, which would codify Roe v Wade into law.

**THEN:** He voted to pass anti-choice legislation that was chock-full of misinformation and had the potential to imprison doctors for just doing their jobs.

Peter, Emily Busch is the pro-choice Democrat running to unseat John James and be a strong voice for the issues that matter to our community.

[**You can help our team share this message with voters across the district with a donation of any amount you can spare. Ahead of our End of Month Fundraising Deadline, can we count on your support to raise the $2,077 we have left to reach our goal?**](https://milwaukeedems.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e61dc0cbc36b6b9ece6e4cb38&id=3962ffe03e&e=4d37f34e0f)

Team Emily Busch

| | | Emily first learned the importance of community and helping others from her mom, a nurse, and dad, a manufacturing representative, while growing up in a tight-knit, middle-class Midwestern family.

The proud product of public schools, Emily worked hard in and out of the classroom, balancing her studies and interest in performing arts with an after-school job as a cashier at Ace Hardware. She went on to earn her B.A. in Biology from Indiana University and Masters from Michigan State University.

Now, Emily is running for Congress in Michigan’s 10th District to keep our kids safe, protect our rights, and lower costs for Michigan families.

Emily chose to move to Oakland County two decades ago because it was the place she wanted to raise her family – a place with friendly neighbors, good schools, and safe neighborhoods.

She and her husband, a retired firefighter and Marine, enjoy camping, fishing, and visiting national parks in their free time.
